entities.name: John the Baptist
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John the Baptist (c. 6 BCE – c. 29 CE): A Jewish prophet who prepared the way for Jesus by preaching repentance and baptizing in the Jordan River. Identified as the fulfillment of Malachi's prophecy of a returned Elijah.

This pivotal figure played a crucial role in shaping the religious landscape of ancient Palestine, influencing the trajectory of Christianity and Judaism. His message of repentance and spiritual renewal resonated with a diverse audience, transcending social and economic boundaries.

The execution of John the Baptist at the hands of Herod Antipas in 29 CE marked a turning point in his life's work, yet his legacy continued to inspire and provoke throughout history. As a symbol of martyrdom and spiritual courage, John the Baptist remains an enduring figure in Christian theology and iconography.

Like many prophets throughout history, John's significance is underscored by a singular, haunting statistic: he was beheaded at the age of 33, a fate that would become a recurring motif in the lives of several other notable figures, including Jesus himself.
